questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Which of the following elements is classified exclusively as a non-metal under standard conditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen** is classified exclusively as a **non-metal** under standard conditions. It is the simplest and lightest element in the periodic table, with an atomic number of 1.
 
• Hydrogen is unique because it exists as a **gas** under standard temperature and pressure (STP) and forms diatomic molecules (H₂).
 
• Unlike metals such as **Zinc**, **Silver**, or **Mercury**, hydrogen does not exhibit metallic properties like malleability, ductility, or electrical conductivity under standard conditions.
 
• Hydrogen is chemically reactive and combines with many elements to form compounds, such as water (H₂O) and hydrogen chloride (HCl).
 
• It is placed at the top of Group 1 in the periodic table but is not considered an alkali metal due to its non-metallic nature and unique chemical behavior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zinc:**

 
 
• Zinc is a **metal** and belongs to Group 12 of the periodic table.
 
• It is a transition metal with properties like malleability, ductility, and electrical conductivity.
 
• Zinc is commonly used for galvanization to prevent rusting of iron and steel.
 
 
 
• **Silver:**
 
 
• Silver is a **precious metal** known for its high electrical and thermal conductivity.
 
• It is widely used in jewelry, coins, and industrial applications like electronics.
 
• Silver is part of the transition metals and is found in Group 11 of the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Mercury:**
 
 
• Mercury is a **metal** that is unique for being in a liquid state at room temperature.
 
• It is used in thermometers, barometers, and fluorescent lights due to its physical properties.
 
• Mercury is toxic and requires careful handling.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen:**
 
 
• Hydrogen is the most **abundant element** in the universe, making up about 75% of its elemental mass.
 
• It is used as a fuel in hydrogen-powered vehicles and plays a critical role in industrial processes like ammonia production (Haber process).
 
• Hydrogen isotopes include **protium** (most common), **deuterium**, and **tritium**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Non-Metal Characteristics:**

 
 
• Non-metals are typically poor conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• They exhibit high electronegativity and ionization energy.
 
• Non-metals are brittle in solid form and do not exhibit luster.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Placement:**
 
 
• Non-metals are primarily located on the right side of the periodic table.
 
• Hydrogen is an exception as it is placed at the top of Group 1 but does not belong to the alkali metal family.

questions.question: The energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential energy** is the energy possessed by a body due to its **position, configuration, or state**. It is stored energy that is ready to be converted into other forms, such as kinetic energy.
 
• Potential energy is often associated with a body’s position relative to other objects or a force field, such as the **gravitational field**. For example, a ball at a certain height has gravitational potential energy.
 
• The formula for gravitational potential energy is **U = mgh**, where **m** is the mass, **g** is the acceleration due to gravity, and **h** is the height.
 
• Potential energy can also be elastic in nature, such as the energy stored in a **compressed spring**. This is called elastic potential energy.
 
• Potential energy is a form of **mechanical energy** and is different from kinetic energy, which depends on the motion of the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thermal energy:**

 
 
• Thermal energy refers to the internal energy of a system due to the **random motion of its particles**. It is associated with heat.
 
• It is measured in terms of temperature and is transferred from a hotter object to a cooler one.
 
• An example of thermal energy is the heat produced by a stove while cooking food.
 
 
 
• **Chemical energy:**
 
 
• Chemical energy is the energy stored in the **bonds of chemical compounds**. It is released during chemical reactions.
 
• Examples include the energy stored in fuels like gasoline or in food, which is converted into usable energy during digestion.
 
• Batteries also store chemical energy, which is converted into electrical energy during use.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic energy:**
 
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion. It is given by the formula **K.E. = ½ mv²**, where **m** is the mass and **v** is the velocity.
 
• Examples include a moving car, a flying airplane, or flowing water in a river.
 
• Kinetic energy depends on the speed and mass of the object. Faster-moving or heavier objects have higher kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Applications of potential energy:**
 
 
• Potential energy is used in **hydropower plants**, where water stored at a height is converted into kinetic energy to generate electricity.
 
• Elastic potential energy is used in devices like **springs, catapults, and trampolines**.
 
• Gravitational potential energy plays a key role in **roller coasters**, pendulums, and projectiles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Conversion:**

 
 
• Potential energy can be converted into other forms of energy, such as kinetic energy during motion or into thermal energy due to friction.
 
• For example, when a ball falls from a height, its gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• Energy is neither created nor destroyed; it only **changes forms**. The total energy in a closed system remains constant.
 
• This principle ensures that potential energy is converted into other forms without any loss, barring external forces like friction.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy in Space:**
 
 
• Gravitational potential energy varies with **distance from the center** of the Earth or other celestial bodies.
 
• It plays a crucial role in orbital mechanics and satellite launches.

questions.question: Covalent bonds are formed by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sharing of electrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Covalent bonds** are formed when two atoms share **electrons** in order to achieve a stable electronic configuration, resembling the nearest noble gas.
 
• This sharing of electrons allows both atoms to fill their **outermost shell**, or valence shell, achieving stability.
 
• The number of shared electron pairs determines the type of covalent bond: **single bond** (1 pair), **double bond** (2 pairs), or **triple bond** (3 pairs).
 
• **Nonmetals** are typically involved in covalent bonding because they have similar electronegativities, making it energetically favorable to share electrons.
 
• Examples of covalent bonds include molecules like **H₂ (Hydrogen gas)**, **O₂ (Oxygen gas)**, **CH₄ (Methane)**, and **H₂O (Water)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Covalent Bonds:**

 
 
• Covalent bonds are generally strong due to the close sharing of electrons between atoms.
 
• Molecules with covalent bonds often have low **melting** and **boiling points** because they consist of discrete molecules held together by weaker intermolecular forces (e.g., van der Waals forces or hydrogen bonds).
 
• Covalent compounds are typically poor conductors of electricity because they lack free electrons or ions.
 
 
 
• **Differences from Ionic Bonds:**
 
 
• In ionic bonds, electrons are **transferred** from one atom to another, creating charged ions that attract each other.
 
• Covalent bonds involve **sharing** of electrons rather than transfer, resulting in neutral molecules.
 
• Ionic compounds generally have higher melting and boiling points compared to covalent compounds.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Covalent Compounds:**
 
 
• **Water (H₂O):** Oxygen shares electrons with two hydrogen atoms to form a bent molecular structure.
 
• **Carbon dioxide (CO₂):** Carbon forms two double bonds with two oxygen atoms, creating a linear molecule.
 
• **Methane (CH₄):** Carbon shares electrons with four hydrogen atoms to form a tetrahedral structure.
 
 
 
• **Types of Covalent Bonds:**
 
 
• **Non-polar covalent bond:** Electrons are shared equally between atoms (e.g., H₂, O₂).
 
• **Polar covalent bond:** Electrons are shared unequally due to a difference in electronegativity (e.g., H₂O).
 
 
 
• **Significance of Covalent Bonds:**
 
 
• They are essential for the structure and function of biological molecules like **proteins**, **DNA**, and **lipids**.
 
• Covalent bonding is fundamental to organic chemistry, which studies compounds primarily composed of carbon and hydrogen.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the centre of curvature of a spherical mirror is NOT true?

options.text: It lies outside the reflecting surface of the mirror.
For a concave mirror, it is located behind the mirror.
It is not a part of the mirror itself.
For a convex mirror, it lies behind the mirror.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**For a concave mirror, it is located behind the mirror.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **centre of curvature** of a spherical mirror is defined as the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part. It is represented by the letter **C**.
 
• **Statement 1:** It lies outside the reflecting surface of the mirror. **This statement is correct** because the center of curvature is always located at a point outside the mirror, on the principal axis.
 
• **Statement 2:** For a concave mirror, it is located behind the mirror. **This statement is incorrect** as the center of curvature for a concave mirror lies in front of the reflecting surface, not behind it.
 
• **Statement 3:** It is not a part of the mirror itself. **This statement is correct** since the center of curvature is a geometric point and does not lie on the mirror's surface

questions.question: Which element has mass number 27 and 14 neutrons present in it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mass number** is the sum of protons and neutrons in an atom. Here, the mass number is 27, and the element has 14 neutrons.
 
• The number of protons in an atom is equal to its atomic number. To find the atomic number: **Mass number = Protons + Neutrons**.
 
• For this element: **27 = Protons + 14**, which means the atomic number (protons) is **13**.
 
• The element with atomic number 13 is **Aluminium**. Hence, the correct answer is Aluminium.
 
• Aluminium is represented by the symbol **Al**, with an atomic number of 13 and a standard atomic mass of approximately 27 u.

questions.question: Which mirror is used by a dentist to see the inside of a patient’s mouth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **concave mirror** is used by dentists to examine the inside of a patient’s mouth because it produces a **magnified and upright image** of the object when placed within its focal length.
 
• When a concave mirror is used at a close distance (within the focal length), it creates a **virtual and enlarged image** of the teeth, allowing the dentist to observe fine details.
 
• The **curved surface** of the concave mirror collects and focuses light onto the area being examined, enhancing visibility in the usually dimly lit oral cavity.
 
• This type of mirror is ideal for precision tasks such as identifying cavities, cracks, or gum problems, as the enlarged reflection provides a clearer view.
 
• Other types of mirrors, such as convex or plane mirrors, do not produce magnified images, making them unsuitable for dental examinations.

questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius 1.5 {m} with angular velocity 3 {rad/s} . What will the ratio of its linear velocity to angular velocity be?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __** 2 : 1 **__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The linear velocity ( v ) of a particle moving in a circle is related to its angular velocity ( omega ) by the formula ** v = r · omega **, where r is the radius of the circle. • In this case, the radius of the circle is **1.5 m**, and the angular velocity is **3 rad/s**. • Substituting the values into the formula: ** v = 1.5 · 3 = 4.5 {m/s} **. • The ratio of the particle's linear velocity to angular velocity can be calculated as v : omega = 4.5 : 3 . • Upon simplification, the ratio becomes 2 : 1 . **Hence, the correct answer is 2 : 1 .**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of short-duration crop varieties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Higher chances of crop damage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Short-duration crop varieties** are bred to mature faster, allowing multiple harvests in a year. This feature enables **multiple cropping** and ensures higher productivity. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• Since these crops grow and mature quickly, they require fewer inputs like water, fertilizers, and labor, resulting in **reduced production costs**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• Quick harvesting facilitates efficient utilization of agricultural land and minimizes idle periods, making it easier to manage resources and improve profitability. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• However, it is incorrect to say that short-duration crop varieties have a higher chance of crop damage. In fact, their shorter lifecycle often helps them escape adverse weather conditions or pest attacks that affect long-duration crops. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Benefits of short-duration crops:**

 
 
• They enable **crop diversification**, allowing farmers to grow different types of crops within a year.
 
• They are particularly beneficial in regions with **short growing seasons**, such as areas with limited rainfall or extreme climatic conditions.
 
• Short-duration crops reduce the risk of pest and disease outbreaks due to their **short lifecycle**.
 
• Examples include crops like **millets, pulses, and certain varieties of rice** that mature within 90-120 days.
 
 
 
• **Multiple cropping systems:**
 
 
• Multiple cropping involves growing two or more crops sequentially or simultaneously on the same land during a single growing season.
 
• It maximizes land usage and enhances **farm income**.
 
• Short-duration crops are ideal for multiple cropping as they leave sufficient time between harvests for subsequent crops.
 
 
 
• **Reduced production costs:**
 
 
• Short-duration crops often require less water, fertilizers, and pesticides, lowering the overall **input costs**.
 
• Labor requirements are also reduced due to their shorter cultivation period, making them economical for small-scale farmers.
 
 
 
• **Quick harvesting:**
 
 
• Short-duration crops allow farmers to harvest quickly, enabling better **land management** and preparation for subsequent crops.
 
• They are particularly useful in regions prone to **climatic uncertainties**, as farmers can adapt to changing conditions more effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Crop damage risks:**

 
 
• Contrary to the statement, short-duration crops often avoid prolonged exposure to adverse conditions, reducing the risk of damage.
 
• Long-duration crops are more vulnerable to prolonged droughts, floods, or pest infestations.
 
 
 
• **Examples of short-duration crops:**
 
 
• Certain varieties of rice like **Sahbhagi Dhan**, which matures in 90 days, are popular among Indian farmers.
 
• Other examples include millets, pulses, and vegetables like **radish and spinach**.

questions.question:
Read the following statements carefully and select the correct option.

Assertion (A): In the reaction of copper with oxygen, oxygen acts as the reducing agent.

Reason (R): Oxygen adds to copper forming copper oxide.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is false, but R is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A):** The statement that “In the reaction of copper with oxygen, oxygen acts as the reducing agent” is **false**. Oxygen cannot act as a reducing agent because it undergoes reduction itself by gaining electrons during the formation of copper oxide.
 
• **Reason (R):** The statement that “Oxygen adds to copper forming copper oxide” is **true**. In this reaction, oxygen reacts with copper, resulting in the formation of copper oxide (CuO).
 
• In a redox reaction, the substance that loses electrons is the reducing agent, while the substance that gains electrons is the oxidizing agent. In this case, **oxygen acts as the oxidizing agent**, not the reducing agent.
 
• The process involves copper (Cu) being oxidized to copper ions (Cu²⁺) while oxygen is reduced to oxide ions (O²⁻). This confirms that oxygen is the oxidizing agent.
 
• Since the assertion (A) incorrectly states the role of oxygen in the reaction, it is **false**, but the reason (R), which correctly describes the formation of copper oxide, is **true**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxidation and Reduction:**

 
 
• **Oxidation:** It refers to the loss of electrons or the addition of oxygen to a substance. For example, copper (Cu) is oxidized to Cu²⁺ ions in this reaction.
 
• **Reduction:** It refers to the gain of electrons or the removal of oxygen from a substance. For example, oxygen (O₂) is reduced to O²⁻ ions in this reaction.
 
 
 
• **Role of Agents:**
 
 
• **Reducing Agent:** A substance that donates electrons and gets oxidized in the process. In this reaction, copper acts as the reducing agent.
 
• **Oxidizing Agent:** A substance that accepts electrons and gets reduced in the process. In this reaction, oxygen acts as the oxidizing agent.
 
 
 
• **Copper Oxide Formation:**
 
 
• Copper reacts with oxygen to form copper oxide (CuO). The reaction can be represented as: Cu + O₂ → CuO
 
• The reaction is an example of a redox process, where both oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Copper Oxide:**
 
 
• Copper oxide is widely used in applications such as semiconductors, catalysts, and pigments.
 
• It is also used in the manufacturing of antifouling paints and as a precursor for producing other copper compounds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Reactions:** Redox reactions are crucial in understanding the exchange of electrons between substances and determining their roles as oxidizing or reducing agents.
 
• **Common Misconceptions:** It is essential to correctly identify the oxidizing and reducing agents in a reaction to avoid confusion.
 
• **Industrial Relevance:** Redox reactions are fundamental to processes like corrosion prevention, metal extraction, and energy production in batteries.
 
• **Scientific Terminology:** Terms like “oxidation” and “reduction” are often used interchangeably with “electron transfer,” emphasizing the role of electrons in chemical processes.

questions.question: Which of the following organs is a part of the human female reproductive system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uterus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **uterus** is a major organ in the **female reproductive system**. It is where a fertilized egg implants and develops into a fetus during pregnancy.
 
• It is a hollow, muscular organ located in the **pelvic region** of females, between the bladder and rectum.
 
• The uterus is composed of three layers: **endometrium** (inner lining), **myometrium** (muscular layer), and **perimetrium** (outer layer).
 
• Its primary functions include **supporting fetal development**, facilitating childbirth through its strong muscular contractions, and shedding its lining during menstruation if fertilization does not occur.
 
• The uterus plays a crucial role in the **reproductive cycle**, including ovulation, fertilization, and the menstrual cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prostate Gland:**

 
 
• The prostate gland is part of the **male reproductive system** and is not present in females.
 
• It is responsible for producing a fluid that nourishes and transports sperm during ejaculation.
 
• The gland is located below the bladder and surrounds the urethra in males.
 
 
 
• **Vas Deferens:**
 
 
• The vas deferens is another component of the **male reproductive system**.
 
• It serves as a duct that transports sperm from the epididymis to the urethra during ejaculation.
 
• This organ is absent in females.
 
 
 
• **Testis:**
 
 
• The testis (plural: testes) is a male reproductive organ responsible for producing sperm and the hormone **testosterone**.
 
• It is located in the scrotum, outside the male body, for maintaining an optimal temperature for sperm production.
 
• Females do not have testes; instead, they have ovaries, which produce eggs and hormones like estrogen and progesterone.
 
 
 
• **Female Reproductive System Overview:**
 
 
• The female reproductive system includes organs such as the **ovaries**, **fallopian tubes**, **uterus**, **vagina**, and **external genitalia**.
 
• Its primary functions are the production of eggs (ova), facilitation of fertilization, and support for fetal development during pregnancy.
 
• The ovaries release eggs during ovulation, which travel through the fallopian tubes to the uterus.
 
• If fertilization occurs, the fertilized egg implants in the uterus and begins to develop into an embryo.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Menstrual Cycle:** The uterus plays a vital role in the menstrual cycle. If fertilization does not occur, the endometrium is shed, leading to menstruation.
 
• **Pregnancy:** The uterus expands significantly during pregnancy to accommodate the growing fetus and contracts during childbirth to aid delivery.
 
• **Common Disorders:** Some common uterine disorders include fibroids, endometriosis, uterine prolapse, and cancer. These conditions may affect fertility and overall reproductive health.
 
• **Ovaries vs. Uterus:** While ovaries produce eggs and hormones, the uterus is primarily responsible for supporting pregnancy and facilitating childbirth.

questions.question: An object floats on water if ________.

• **Density** is defined as the mass per unit volume (**ρ = m/V**). For an object to float, its density must be lower than water so that the upward buoyant force counteracts its downward gravitational force.
 
• This phenomenon is explained by **Archimedes' Principle**, which states that "a body immersed in a fluid experiences a buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it."
 
• If the density of the object is **greater than water**, the object sinks because the gravitational force exceeds the buoyant force.

questions.question: How long does an unfertilised egg typically survive in the female reproductive tract?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24 hours**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• After **ovulation**, the egg is released from the **ovary** and travels through the **fallopian tube**, where it awaits fertilization.
 
• If the egg is not fertilized within **24 hours**, it begins to disintegrate and is absorbed by the body. Hence, fertilization must occur within this timeframe.
 
• In contrast to the egg’s short survival time, **sperm** can survive in the female reproductive tract for up to **5 days**, which increases the chances of fertilization if intercourse occurs in the days leading up to ovula

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct?

options.text: Multiple reflections change the pitch of sound
Multiple reflections improve sound distribution in large halls
Multiple reflections are undesirable in small rooms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Multiple reflections change the pitch of sound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reverberation:** Multiple reflections of sound in a space cause reverberation, where sound persists for a while after the source stops. Reverberation is common in large spaces like concert halls or auditoriums. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***
 
• **Pitch of Sound:** The pitch of a sound is determined by its frequency, not by the number of reflections. Multiple reflections may amplify or sustain the sound but do not alter its frequency or pitch. ***Hence, this statement is NOT correct.***
 
• **Sound Distribution in Large Halls:** Multiple reflections are often desirable in large spaces to distribute sound evenly, ensuring that the audience can hear the sound clearly from any location. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***
 
• **Undesirability in Small Rooms:** In small enclosed spaces, multiple reflections can lead to excessive reverberation, causing distortion of sound, which is undesirable. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reverberation Time:** Reverberation time is the duration it takes for the sound to decay by 60 dB after the source stops. It depends on the size of the room and the materials used in its construction.
 
• **Applications of Reverberation:**
 
 
• In concert halls, controlled reverberation enhances the quality and richness of music.
 
• In lecture halls, excessive reverberation is avoided to maintain clarity of speech.
 
 
 
• **Pitch of Sound:** The pitch is related to the frequency of the sound wave. Higher frequency results in a higher pitch, while lower frequency results in a lower pitch. Factors like the source of vibration and tension in the vibrating medium influence the frequency but not reflections.
 
• **Echo vs. Reverberation:** Echo is a distinct repetition of sound after a delay (greater than 0.1 seconds), while reverberation is the overlapping of sound reflections without a distinct delay.
 
• **Acoustic Treatment:** To control undesirable multiple reflections, acoustic materials like foam panels, carpets, or curtains are used in spaces like recording studios or small rooms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sound Reflection Applications:** Reflection of sound is used in technologies like sonar, ultrasonic imaging, and echo-based distance measurement.
 
• **Reverberation Control:** In spaces like theaters or conference rooms, the reverberation time is optimized to ensure clarity and richness of sound.
 
• **Human Hearing Range:** Humans can hear sounds with frequencies between 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. The pitch of sound within this range is perceived based on frequency, not reflections.
 
• **Acoustic Design:** Proper acoustic design involves balancing absorption and reflection to achieve the desired sound quality in a space.

questions.question: In a starch test using a variegated leaf, what is the purpose of adding iodine solution at the end?

options.text: To remove chlorophyll from green areas
To identify the areas without chloroplasts
To stain the starch present in the leaf

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To stain the starch present in the leaf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **purpose of adding iodine solution** in a starch test is to **identify the presence of starch** in the leaf by staining it. Iodine reacts with starch to produce a **blue-black coloration**, which confirms the presence of starch.
 
• This test is usually conducted after **boiling the leaf in alcohol** to remove chlorophyll, making the starch test results more visible.
 
• The **blue-black coloration** appears only in areas of the leaf where starch is present, which is usually in the green areas containing chlorophyll, as photosynthesis occurs there.
 
• The iodine solution serves as a **staining agent** and does not dissolve or remove starch; its role is purely to highlight starch presence through a visible color change.
 
• This test is significant in experiments to demonstrate that **photosynthesis produces starch** and to determine which parts of the leaf are photosynthetically active.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Steps in the Starch Test:**

 
 
• **Pluck a variegated leaf** (a leaf with both green and non-green areas).
 
• Boil the leaf in water to **kill the cells**.
 
• Boil the leaf in alcohol to **remove chlorophyll** and decolorize it.
 
• Rinse the leaf in warm water to soften it.
 
• Add iodine solution to the leaf and observe the color change.
 
 
 
• **Role of Different Steps:**
 
 
• **Boiling in water:** This step stops all metabolic processes in the leaf by killing the cells.
 
• **Boiling in alcohol:** This removes chlorophyll, making the leaf colorless and allowing the iodine-starch reaction to be visible.
 
• **Adding iodine:** This stains the starch present in the leaf, producing a blue-black color.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Variegated Leaf:** A variegated leaf has both green (chlorophyll-containing) and non-green areas. This allows scientists to demonstrate that starch is synthesized only in the green parts, where photosynthesis occurs.
 
• **Why Starch is Tested:** Starch is a storage form of glucose produced during photosynthesis. Testing for starch indirectly confirms that photosynthesis has occurred in the green areas of the leaf.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chlorophyll and Photosynthesis:** Chlorophyll is essential for photosynthesis, which occurs only in green areas of the leaf. The non-green areas do not photosynthesize and thus do not produce starch.
 
• **Iodine-Starch Reaction:** Iodine reacts with starch molecules to form a blue-black complex, which is visible and confirms the presence of starch.
 
• **Demonstration of Photosynthesis:** This experiment is a classic method used in biology to demonstrate that photosynthesis occurs only in green chlorophyll-containing regions.
 
• **Other Uses of Iodine:** Apart from the starch test, iodine is also used as an antiseptic and in medical imaging as a contrast agent.
 
• **Significance:** This test helps in understanding plant physiology and the role of chlorophyll in food production, contributing to foundational knowledge in botany and agriculture.

questions.question: Which of the following is a crop variety improvement method by introducing a gene that would provide the desired characteristics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Genetically modified crops**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Genetically modified crops (GM crops)** are developed by introducing a specific gene or set of genes into the plant's genome to provide desired characteristics such as resistance to pests, diseases, or environmental conditions.
 
• The process involves **transferring genes** from one organism (which could be a plant, bacterium, or another species) into the target crop through genetic engineering techniques like recombinant DNA technology.
 
• **Desired traits** in GM crops include increased yield, improved nutritional content, resistance to herbicides, and tolerance to drought or salinity.
 
• Examples of genetically modified crops include **Bt cotton** (resistant to bollworms), **Golden rice** (enhanced with Vitamin A), and **herbicide-tolerant soybean**.
 
• This method is more precise and quicker compared to traditional breeding techniques, as the desired traits can be introduced without affecting other characteristics of the crop.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Grafting**:

 
 
• This is a traditional horticultural technique where tissues of plants are joined together to continue their growth as one plant.
 
• It is commonly used to propagate plants with desired characteristics, but it does not involve genetic modification at the DNA level.
 
• Example: Grafting is widely used in fruit-bearing plants like apple and citrus trees.
 
 
 
• **Budding**:
 
 
• Budding is a form of grafting where a single bud from the desired plant is inserted into the rootstock of another plant.
 
• It is primarily used in the propagation of ornamental plants and fruit trees.
 
• Unlike genetic modification, it does not involve introducing foreign genes into the plant.
 
 
 
• **Natural vegetative reproduction**:
 
 
• This is a natural process where plants reproduce using parts like roots, stems, or leaves without seeds.
 
• Examples include the growth of new plants from potato tubers or onion bulbs.
 
• This method does not involve any genetic engineering or artificial intervention.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Genetically Modified Crops:**
 
 
• Higher crop yields and reduced dependency on chemical pesticides.
 
• Improved nutritional content, such as biofortified crops.
 
• Resistance to abiotic stresses like drought and salinity.
 
• Reduced agricultural costs and increased farmer profitability.
 
 
 
• **Challenges and Concerns:**
 
 
• Potential environmental impacts such as the development of resistant pests and loss of biodiversity.
 
• Ethical and health concerns about consuming genetically modified organisms (GMOs).
 
• Regulatory hurdles and public resistance in some countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bt Cotton:** The first genetically modified crop introduced in India in 2002, designed to resist bollworm pests.
 
• **Golden Rice:** Genetically modified to produce beta-carotene, a precursor to Vitamin A, aimed at combating Vitamin A deficiency in developing countries.
 
• **Regulatory Framework in India:** The **Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC)** under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is responsible for approving GM crops for commercial use.
 
• **Global Adoption:** Countries like the **USA, Brazil, and Argentina** are leaders in GM crop cultivation, with crops like GM soybean, maize, and cotton widely grown.

questions.question: Why is a transportation system essential for excretion in multicellular organisms?

options.text: To move waste products to the organs that remove them

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To move waste products to the organs that remove them**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Excretion** is a vital biological process in multicellular organisms to remove metabolic waste products such as urea, carbon dioxide, and excess salts from the body.
 
• In multicellular organisms, the **transportation system plays a central role** in the excretion process by ensuring the movement of waste products from cells to excretory organs like kidneys, lungs, and skin.
 
• The circulatory system, comprising **blood and lymphatic vessels**, transports nitrogenous wastes like urea and uric acid from tissues to the kidneys for filtration and elimination.
 
• This system ensures that waste products do not accumulate in the body, preventing **toxic buildup** that can disrupt cellular functions and harm the organism.
 
• Without a transportation system, waste products would remain localized in tissues, leading to **inefficiency in detoxification** and a higher risk of diseases or metabolic imbalances.

questions.question: What is associated with a metallic wire carrying an electric current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A magnetic field around it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **electric current** flows through a **metallic wire**, it generates a **magnetic field** around it. This phenomenon is explained by **Oersted's experiment**, which demonstrated the relationship between electricity and magnetism.
 
• The **magnetic field** forms concentric circles around the wire, and its direction is determined by the **right-hand thumb rule**: if the thumb points in the direction of the current, the curled fingers indicate the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field depends on the **magnitude of the current** passing through the wire and the **distance** from the wire. It decreases as the distance increases.
 
• This property of a current-carrying wire is utilized in various applications, such as in the working of **electromagnets**, **electric motors**, and **generators**.
 
• The generation of a magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor is a fundamental concept in **electromagnetism**, forming the basis for many technological advancements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Current and Magnetic Field:**

 
 
• The connection between electricity and magnetism was first discovered by **Hans Christian Oersted** in **1820**, who found that a compass needle deflects when placed near a current-carrying conductor.
 
• This discovery laid the foundation for the field of **electromagnetism**, which combines the study of electric and magnetic phenomena.
 
 
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the **direction of the magnetic field** created by a current-carrying wire.
 
• To apply the rule, point the **thumb** of your right hand in the direction of the current, and the curl of your fingers will show the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Applications:**
 
 
• Electromagnets, which are used in devices like **electric bells**, **relays**, and **MRI machines**, operate based on the principle of a magnetic field induced by an electric current.
 
• Electric motors and generators also rely on this principle to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy (or vice versa).
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field Strength:**
 
 
• The strength of the magnetic field is directly proportional to the **current** through the wire and inversely proportional to the **distance** from the wire.
 
• Mathematically, the magnetic field (B) due to a straight current-carrying conductor is given by **B = (μ₀I)/(2πr)**, where μ₀ is the permeability of free space, I is the current, and r is the radial distance from the wire.
 
 
 
• **Heat and Resistance in Wires:**
 
 
• Although a current-carrying wire generates heat due to **electrical resistance**, this is not the primary phenomenon associated with the question's context.
 
• The heat generated follows **Joule's law of heating**, where heat (H) is proportional to the square of the current (I²), resistance (R), and time (t).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: Only Electric Potential**:

 
 
• While an electric current is associated with **electric potential**, this is not the primary effect in the context of the question.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: A Magnetic Field Around It**:
 
 
• This is the **correct answer**, as a magnetic field is always produced around a current-carrying conductor.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Only Heat**:
 
 
• A wire carrying current does generate heat due to resistance, but this is not the main phenomenon described here.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: No Physical Effect**:
 
 
• This is incorrect because a current-carrying wire has multiple physical effects, including the generation of a magnetic field and heat.

questions.question: If both current and resistance are halved, the power reduces to _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-fourth of the initial value**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power in an electrical circuit** is given by the formula: **P = I²R**, where **P** is the power, **I** is the current, and **R** is the resistance.
 
• If both the current (**I**) and resistance (**R**) are halved, the new power can be calculated as follows:
 
 
• Let the initial values of current and resistance be **I** and **R**.
 
• Initial Power: **P = I²R**.
 
• When the current is halved, the new current becomes **I/2**.
 
• When the resistance is halved, the new resistance becomes **R/2**.
 
• New Power: **P' = (I/2)² × (R/2)**.
 
• Expanding the equation: **P' = (I²/4) × (R/2) = I²R/8.**
 
 
 
• Comparing the new power (**P'**) with the initial power (**P**), we get: **P' = P/4**.
 
• This means the power is reduced to **one-fourth** of its initial value.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **one-fourth of the initial value**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrical Power:**

 
 
• Electrical power is the rate at which electrical energy is transferred by an electric circuit.
 
• It is measured in **watts (W)**, where 1 watt = 1 joule/second.
 
• The mathematical formulas for power are:
 
 
• **P = IV**, where **I** is current and **V** is voltage.
 
• **P = I²R**, where **R** is resistance.
 
• **P = V²/R**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Current and Resistance Relationship:**
 
 
• Current (**I**) and resistance (**R**) are inversely proportional when the voltage is constant, as per Ohm's Law: **I = V/R**.
 
• Changes in resistance and current significantly affect power, as seen in the formulas above.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding power reduction is critical in designing energy-efficient electrical systems.
 
• For example, halving current and resistance is often practiced in electronic circuits to manage power consumption effectively.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Power Calculation:**
 
 
• Example 1: If a circuit has an initial current of 4 A and resistance of 8 ohms, the power is **P = I²R = 4² × 8 = 128 W**. If both current and resistance are halved, new power is **P' = (2² × 4) = 32 W**, which is one-fourth of the initial power.
 
• Example 2: For a circuit with initial current 10 A and resistance 20 ohms, power is **P = 10² × 20 = 2000 W**. After halving both, new power is **P' = (5² × 10) = 500 W**, again one-fourth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:** It states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided the temperature remains constant.
 
• **Units of Power:** Power is measured in **watts (W)**. Larger units include kilowatts (1 kW = 1000 W) and megawatts (1 MW = 10⁶ W).
 
• **Applications:** Power calculations are used in electrical engineering, energy management, and electronics design.
 
• **Concept of Efficiency:** Efficiency is the ratio of output power to input power, often expressed as a percentage.
